new_statements.quote: O sistema prosódico do Baniwa-Curripaco (dialeto central) é simples: o acento de altura cai sempre na sílaba que precede imediatamente a última sílaba métrica da palavra. Em outras palavras, o sistema prosódico é um sistema misto de acentuação lexical, com a existência de sufixos extramétricos (a metricidade de cada sufixo é dada pelo dicionário) e de acentuação pós-lexical (com o acento na sílaba que precede imediatamente a última sílaba métrica, como uma língua de acento fixo). [p. 88:] Nesta secção, estudaremos o acento e o seu assinalamento em Baniwa-Curripaco. Limitaremo-nos ao dialeto central e ao acento primário.
new_statements.translation: The prosodic system of Baniwa-Curripaco (central dialect) is simple: the pitch accent always falls on the syllable immediately preceding the last metrical syllable of the word. In other words, the prosodic system is a mixed system of lexical accentuation, with extrametrical suffixes (the metricality of each suffix is given by the dictionary), and post-lexical accentuation (with the accent on the syllable immediately preceding the last metrical syllable, like a fixed-accent language). [p. 88:] In this section we study accent and its assignment in Baniwa-Curripaco. We limit ourselves to the central dialect and to primary accent.
new_statements.citation: Ramirez, Henri. 2001. Línguas Arawak da Amazônia Setentrional: comparação e descrição. Manaus: Editora da Universidade do Amazonas (EDUA). Ch. 2 'Baniwa-Curripaco e Tariano', sec. 2.1.1 point 10 (p. 46) and sec. 2.1.5 'Acentuação' (pp. 88-96).

Printed p. 88, sec. 2.1.5 Acentu…
new_statements.rule_in_words: One pitch accent per phonological word, on the syllable (mora, since long vowels/diphthongs count as two syllables) immediately before the last metrical syllable; with a metrical final syllable this is the penult, and the accent never falls on the final syllable. Certain outer suffixes (e.g. -ka subordinator, all object-person suffixes) are extrametrical and invisible to the rule, so surface accent can sit further left; extrametricality is lexically listed per suffix.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not treated by Ramirez ('Limitaremo-nos.. ao acento primário'). Taylor 1991:18-19 (Aiari Baniwa, held by the project) marks a secondary accent on enclitic object pronouns (rikapa-hnuà) and calls secondary accents an unresolved problem.
new_statements.exceptions: Most onomatopoeias are unaccented (p. 88); the adjectivizer -me is irregular (p. 92); H vs LH melody on heavy accented syllables partly lexical (pp. 94-96). Ramirez's rule box adds that non-metrical syllables are transparent to the rule (p. 89).
new_statements.domain_note: Phonological word (root + suffixes), citation forms and minimal pairs; explicitly the CENTRAL dialect (Huhúdeeni etc., middle Içana/Aiari) of Baniwa-Curripaco. Carútana = Nimuendajú's first (lower-Içana) dialect = Koch-Grünberg's Karútana clans = Ramirez's 'Dialeto Meridional' (now at Victorino, Venezuela), for which Ramirez gives no accent rule.
new_statements.identity_note: caru1240 is a Glottolog bookkeeping entry for the retired ISO code [cru], merged into Baniwa [bwi] = bani1255 (Baniwa do Içana / Baniwa-Kurripako) on 2008-01-14 (CR 2007-006). Carútana (Karútana, Karru) is the lower-Içana dialect: Nimuendajú 1950:169 names it the first of three Baniwa do Içana dialects (Yauareté-, Yuruparí-, Urubú-, Arára-Tapuya clans); its Koch-Grünberg clans (Dzáui-Mínenai) correspond to Ramirez 2001:39 'Dialeto Meridional' (origin lower Içana; today Victorino, rio Guainía, Venezuela). The quoted statement is for the CENTRAL dialect of bani1255, which is already in the catalog; no source describes Carútana stress itself.

sources.note: Pitch accent on the syllable immediately preceding the last metrical syllable of the phonological word (default penult; extrametrical suffixes listed in the dictionary; never final) — but p. 88 restricts the section: 'Limitaremo-nos ao dialeto central e ao acento primário'. Dialect table p. 39: the Carútana-descended lower-Içana clans (Dzawi-Mínanai etc.) form the 'Dialeto Meridional', now spoken at Victorino (Guainía, Venezuela); no separate accent rule is given for it, only accented cited forms (atsínali 'homem', -íinha 'comer').

sources.note: p. 71 stress statement concerns Colombian Kurripako ('El acento es libre.. tiende a recaer en la primera sílaba'), not Carútana. Pp. 61-63 tables: Koch-Grünberg's 'Karútana' clans (Dzáui-Míneaí, Mabátsi-Dákeni, Uátsoli-Dákeni, Déruneí) on the lower Içana; Migliazza 1983:725 equates Içana 'baniwa' with karutana.

sources.citation: Taylor, Gerald. 1991. Introdução à língua baniwa do Içana. Campinas: Editora da UNICAMP. Sec. 2 'O acento tônico', pp. 17-19.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.harvard_location: Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number S.A. T 214 i
sources.note: p. 17: 'O acento tônico em baniwa é essencialmente a pronúncia mais alta de uma das sílabas'; distinctive (píipiri/pipiiri); p. 18: 'o acento "normal" não marcado cai na penúltima sílaba'; secondary stress on object pronouns; author admits no satisfactory analysis. Data from Baniwa speakers of the Aiari (central dialect), not Carútana.

sources.note: Stress section (pp. 185-191) treats Hohodene Baniwa and Kuripako only. Pp. 34-35 (dialect survey) place 'Karru ou Carutana (Venezuela e baixo e médio Içana no Brasil)' as a Baniwa do Içana dialect per Fabre 2005 and derive the ethnonym Karutana from Journet's 'Karrum' (Koch-Grünberg 1911). No Carútana data.
